topic: Compile-Time Polymorphism and Template Metaprogramming: Specialization and Partial Specialization
explanation: Template metaprogramming allows computations to be performed at compile time, leveraging the compiler to generate specialized code based on template parameters.  Partial specialization allows creating variations of a template based on specific combinations of template arguments, enabling fine-grained control over generated code.  This contrasts with runtime polymorphism, where decisions are made during program execution.  Compiler behavior involves sophisticated template instantiation and substitution, impacting code size, performance, and potentially leading to compile-time errors if not handled carefully.  Memory layout depends on the instantiated type; if a partially specialized template leads to a different type than a primary template, this will reflect in different memory layouts.  Assembly-level behavior can vary greatly, showing different instructions and register usage based on the specialized template that is finally instantiated.
